Information Note to the Press (Press Release No.  123 / 2026) 
TELECOM REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA 
www.trai.gov.in 
New Delhi, 28 Sep 2026 
For Immediate Release 
 
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality  along the  Delhi to Agra via Yamuna 
Expressway passing through Dankaur, Jewar, Tappal, Surir, Javara, Baldeo, 
Khandauli, Kuberpur etc . and Agra to Delhi passing through Raja Ki Mandi Jn, 
Mathura Jn, Chata, Kosi Kalan, Palwal, Ballabhgarh,  Faridabad etc. under Delhi 
LSA. 
The Telecom Regulatory  Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of 
Independent Drive Test (IDT)  conducted along the Delhi-Agra Highway route and 
Agra-Delhi Railway route under Delhi LSA, during  the month of Jul 2026, for 
information of general telecom consumers.  The purpose of this drive test is to 
assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) 
provided by Telecom Service Providers  (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures 
performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, 
Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and 
Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and 
encourage TSPs to improve their services. 
2. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network 
performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, 
public transport hubs, etc.  In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions 
are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. 
Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and 
analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems. 
3. TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across Highway 
drive – 183.4 Km, Hotspot location – 01 and Railway Drive – 188 Km during 16th Jul 
2026 to 1 7th Jul 2026 in  Delhi LSA. These tests  were conducted under the  
supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive 
test reports represent the performance of the  TSPs on the area / route under test 
on the day / time of conducting the drive test. 
 
 
 
4. Drive test routes: The map provides overview of drive test routes indicating, hotspot 
test, highway and railway drive route as per the legends shown on the map.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Figure-1: Drive test routes 
 
5.  Key Parameters Assessed 
(a) Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less 
than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 
4G/ 5G). 
 
(b) Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call 
Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS). 
 
(c) Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls. 
 
(d) Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate. 
6. The overall mobile network performance on Delhi to Agra via Yamuna 
Expressway Highway route (Delhi LSA)  for the key parameters has been 
summarized below: - 
a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on 
the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as 
the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total 
samples collected, was 180/13960 for Airtel, 4876/12619 for BSNL, 
145/13268 for RJIL and 44/13327 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps 
have been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
 
 
 

b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), 
measured as the number  of dropped calls out of the number of 
successfully established calls, were 2/65 for Airtel, 16/68 for BSNL, 1/66 
for RJIL and 0/66 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been 
provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
c) Call Silence Instance  - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode 
(5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for 
> 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 16/63 for Airtel, 2/57 
for BSNL, 0/68 for RJIL and 18/68 for VIL. Details of the call silence 
instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
 
d) Data Download and Upload Throughput: 
 
i) Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was 
observed as  135.33 Mbps for  Airtel (5G), 8.10 Mbps for BSNL ( 4G), 
213.68 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 46.48 Mbps for VIL ( 5G). Detail of 
Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
 
ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was 
observed as 17.62 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 3.38 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 20.62 
Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 13.70 Mbps for VIL ( 5G). Details of Upload 
throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
 
Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red 
dot on the map of Annexure-I. 
 
7. The overall mobile network performance on Agra to Delhi Railway route 
(Delhi LSA) for the key parameters has been summarized below: - 
a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on 
the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as 
the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total 
samples collected, was 326/11709 for Airtel, 5264/10895 for BSNL, 
286/11697 for RJIL and 224/11728 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps 
have been provided in the map of Annexure-II. 
 
b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), 
measured as the number  of dropped calls out of the number of 
successfully established calls, were 0/60 for Airtel, 12/60 for BSNL, 3/63 
for RJIL and 2/62 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been 
provided in the map of Annexure-II. 
 
c) Data Download and Upload Throughput: 
 
i) Data Download performance (Overall) : Average download speed 
was observed as 44.23 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 9.99 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 
82.68 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 47.48 Mbps for VIL (5G).  Detail of 
Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-II. 
ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was 
observed as 13.32 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 5.07 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 10.14 
Mbps for RJlL (5G) and 12.31 Mbps for VlL (5G). Details of Upload 
throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-Il. 
Locations of Dropped Calls can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-
II. 
8. Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: - 
a) Highway - The areas covered on the highway drive are Delhi to Agra via 
Yamuna Expressway passing through Dankaur, Jewar, Tappal, Surir, 
Javara, Baldeo, Khandauli, Kuberpur etc. under Delhi LSA. 
b) Hotspot - The hotspot location, capturing stationary user experience is The 
Food Street - Food Court - Yamuna Expressway - Vrindavan Cut. 
c) Railway - The areas covered on the Railway drive are Agra to Delhi 
passing through Raja Ki Mandi in, Math ura in, Chata, Kosi kalan, Pa/wa!, 
Ballabhgarh, Faridabad etc. under Delhi LSA. 
9. The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for 
taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made 
available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional 
information, an email can be sent to adv.ca©trai.gov or Regional Office of TRAI at 
Delhi RO can be contacted on telephone No. +91-11-20907772. 
(Vivek Khare) 
Advisor, RO Delhi, TRA!
